title: Record orchestrator answers to cycle review questions
description: Replace the review fix-limit's unconditional human handoff with one auditable, bounded question/response path owned by the orchestrator role. This first vertical slice applies only when an approved implementation passed its issue verification, independent review returned findings, and the existing first automatic review-fix round has already been used. Add an injectable, transport-neutral RuntimeCycleQuestionResolver. It receives the immutable run id, issue id, workspace, current reviewer finding, prior durable cycle responses, provider id, abort signal and event emitter, and returns exactly `continue` with non-empty guidance or `operator` with the concrete unresolved product/authority ambiguity. Production wires it to a fresh read-only subscription-backed call using that run provider's configured orchestrator model and effort; it must not reuse or pollute the conversational transcript/handoff, reviewer session or executor session. It never edits files, approves, starts or ships. Persist a linked `run.cycle-question` before the call and `run.cycle-response` after it, sharing a generated question id. The response records responder `orchestrator`, adapter source `internal`, typed outcome, public guidance/reason, latency, provider/model/effort and the usage/cost fields the provider actually reports, never hidden reasoning or credentials. A `continue` response is binding guidance to the existing executor session: transition back to working, allow either a precise in-scope fix or an evidence-backed no-change rebuttal, then always re-run issue verification and fresh independent review. An `operator` response enters the existing waiting-user path with the linked question and reason. After the existing first automatic fix, permit at most two orchestrator `continue` responses; a further unresolved review finding, invalid resolver output or an unavailable resolver falls back to waiting-user with the evidence preserved. Derive the budget from durable response events so restart cannot reset it. Provider failures retain the existing typed waiting-provider behavior in review phase; retry may repeat the unresolved question only if no linked response was durably recorded. Extend run cost attribution with an `orchestrator` role so resolver model/effort/tokens/API-equivalent cost join the run total and breakdown without being mistaken for executor, reviewer or subscription charge. Extend round-origin/evaluation replay with a separate orchestrator count and factual resolved-cycle-question count; do not count it as operator intervention or human-attention request, and do not claim causality or invent savings. Surface the response visibly in the existing /runs UI without adding a panel: the correction summary distinguishes orchestrator-resolved rounds, and the Activity row for the linked response carries a localized en-US/pt-BR badge/label that it was an orchestrator answer to the cycle, while preserving public guidance and raw provider/model/effort values. Extend the existing runs workflow/operational catalogs rather than introducing a parallel locale source. Update the existing workflow signals/cohort factual comparison to report orchestrator cycle responses separately from human attention. Extend existing runtime/state/store/evaluation, production-wiring and static-render tests in place to cover: a false-positive no-change response followed by clean review; an in-scope second correction; an explicit semantic ambiguity reaching waiting-user; the two-response ceiling across restart; question/response linkage and retry idempotence; invalid/unavailable resolver safety; provider/model/effort/usage/cost attribution; no operator-intervention inflation; and visible en-US/pt-BR response signals with authored guidance preserved. Preserve the reviewer as independent/read-only, full-verify behavior, approval fingerprint, shipping, proposal capture and bounded run/activity windows. Do not add a table, endpoint, queue, daemon, sidecar, timer, finding regex/classifier, score, third visible model-setting role or MCP implementation. Update HANDOFF.md only to record the stable authority/audit boundary and the resolver port as the future MCP seam; preserve its resilient header, history and approval boundary. Out of scope: full-verify exhaustion, executor-originated questions, automatic provider switching, remote authentication, the pending GSHIP-673 version presentation, other localization and the locale selector.
